items.grounds: CONFIRM at medium (rival-engagement: a defective warrant at an internal tier-1 joint, not alone load-bearing). Re-derived both ways from the staged bytes. (1) The finding's factual ground holds. Every suffix and verb form across oshb:Song.3.6-Song.3.10 is third person: 3fs עֹלָה֙ and מְקֻטֶּ֤רֶת (oshb:Song.3.6, byte tier); 3ms/3fs מִטָּתוֹ֙ ... לָ֑הּ (oshb:Song.3.7, byte tier); 3mp/3ms כֻּלָּם֙ ... חַרְבּוֹ֙ עַל יְרֵכ֔וֹ (oshb:Song.3.8, byte tier); עָ֤שָׂה לוֹ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה (oshb:Song.3.9, byte tier); עַמּוּדָיו֙ ... רְפִידָת֣וֹ ... מֶרְכָּב֖וֹ ... תּוֹכוֹ֙ (oshb:Song.3.10, byte tier). A scan of the pointed bytes of those five verses finds no final-kaf suffix (the only final-kaf tokens are the noun הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ at MT 3:9 and בַּמֶּ֣לֶךְ at MT 3:11), no 1cs -ti perfect, no 1cp -nu form and no independent first- or second-person pronoun; the yod-final tokens are construct plurals (form claims argued from the pointed bytes plus the WEB rendering; no morphology layer is staged). Then oshb:Song.3.11 opens צְאֶ֧ינָה וּֽרְאֶ֛ינָה בְּנ֥וֹת צִיּ֖וֹן (byte tier; WEB “Go out, you daughters of Zion, and see” web:Song.3.11): two feminine-plural imperatives plus the daughters-of-Zion vocative, which the book's voice policy lists by name among its tier-1 formula anchors (adjacent-pair sweep, skeleton tier: 1 verse, MT 3:11; the daughters-of-Jerusalem pair sweeps 7 verses at skeleton tier only because it catches the from-phrase מִבְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם at oshb:Song.3.10, byte tier, which is not an address). So a tier-1-marked rival cut stands at the 3:10|3:11 joint exactly as the finding says. (2) BOTH SIDES of that rival seam weighed from bytes. The preceding verse closes תּוֹכוֹ֙ רָצ֣וּף אַהֲבָ֔ה מִבְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Song.3.10, byte tier) with no parashah seg at MT 3:10 (the WLC inventory's segs in this span sit at MT 3:8 and MT 3:11, single-witness, tier-3; absence is never counterevidence). The following verse continues the same referent after its summons: בַּמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה ... לּ֤וֹ אִמּוֹ֙ ... וּבְי֖וֹם שִׂמְחַ֥ת לִבּֽוֹ (oshb:Song.3.11, byte tier) carries on the 3ms suffix chain of MT 3:9-3:10 and the Shelomo chain שֶׁלִּשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה (oshb:Song.3.7, byte tier) / שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה (oshb:Song.3.9, byte tier) / שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה (oshb:Song.3.11, byte tier) (Shelomo-skeleton sweep: 8 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, one of them the homograph at MT 1:7; 3 of the 8 inside this span). The governing rule that decides: the hybrid granularity permits a cut at a tier-1 marker but does not compel one, and the summons-to-view reads as the unit's own close because its object is the king the description has been building (tier-2 referential continuity, used here only to reject a cut, never to drive a seam), corroborated at tier 3 by the setumah standing AT MT 3:11 rather than at MT 3:10 (single witness). The shipped span is therefore defensible and I propose no respan. (3) The shipped row's defect is real. Its strongest_rejected_alternative rejects two unit_type labels (wasf_poem, narrative_sequence) and names no rival cut; the operative-category law routes exactly that deviation disclosure to device_notes, where the row already carries it, so the rival slot is spent on a duplicate. The row's only engagement of the 3:10|3:11 joint is the device_notes concession that the addressee shift surfaces at the closing imperative, while boundary_rationale treats a marker of the book's own tier-1 class as a unit-internal close without saying why it does not open a unit. That is an unargued warrant at the one internal joint where the book's law demands engagement: a defective warrant, medium. Not high, because both outer seams stand on tier-1 anchors weighed from both sides: front, the full adjuration הִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֜ם בְּנ֤וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ (oshb:Song.3.5, byte tier; setumah at MT 3:5, single-witness tier-3) closes the seek-find episode and מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר (oshb:Song.3.6, byte tier; collates byte against oshb:Song.8.5 as well; ascent-formula sweep, skeleton tier: 2 verses, MT 3:6 and MT 8:5; bare mi-zot interrogative 3 verses, MT 3:6, 6:10, 8:5) opens a fresh 3fs question; rear, MT 3:11 closes on שִׂמְחַ֥ת לִבּֽוֹ (oshb:Song.3.11, byte tier; setumah at MT 3:11, single-witness tier-3) and הִנָּ֨ךְ יָפָ֤ה רַעְיָתִי֙ (oshb:Song.4.1, byte tier) opens the his-word address, coherent with the adjacent shipped rows Song.3.5-Song.3.5 and Song.4.1-Song.4.7, which argue those same seams from their own sides. Not low: this is not a mechanical or register slip but the missing half of the row's own warrant for a six-verse span (the register bleed the auditor folded in, the governance phrase closest-fit operative category inside row prose, is a genuine low-severity component and moves the severity neither way). (4) Repair proposal tested as adversarially as the row: the field repair is byte-sound and is ENDORSED AS A PROPOSAL for owner triage, with this qualification: the replacement sentence should REJECT the 3:10|3:11 cut on the grounds in (2) (the 3ms referential chain and the Shelomo chain binding MT 3:11 to MT 3:9-3:10; the setumah at MT 3:11 disclosed single-witness, tier-3, corroboration only), quoting the pointed onset splice of oshb:Song.3.11 with its byte tier, and leave the deviation disclosure in device_notes; the accept-and-respan branch is not supported by these bytes and is not proposed. Non-span item: span_change false, span_ruling n/a; both sides of every seam in play were weighed from bytes.

CONFIRM at medium (E-05 count-object blend: a false digit at the object named, not load-bearing). Re-derived both ways from the staged bytes. (1) The row's parenthetical names the pointed token הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) as a byte-sweep object and attaches two digits, 1 verse book-wide and 2 occurrences in-verse. Re-swept with each object named: the exact byte token הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית returns 1 verse and 1 token book-wide (in-verse byte count 1); the verse's second epithet token is the bet-prefixed בַּשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier), a different string at byte, accent-stripped and skeleton tier, itself 1 verse / 1 token; only the prefix-tolerant epithet skeleton שולמית (the consonants shared by both tokens; skeleton tier) returns 1 verse / 2 tokens. So the book-wide-uniqueness half is true at every object, while the in-verse digit is false at the byte object the row names and true only at a skeleton object the row does not name: the finding's grounds re-derive exactly, and the shipped formulation is a blended count of the class the book's count discipline forbids. (2) Not load-bearing, established by weighing the seam from both sides. The preceding verse closes in 1cs, לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי נַפְשִׁ֣י שָׂמַ֔תְנִי (oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier; the exegesis note at MT 6:12 is single-witness apparatus), and the seam verse opens on the fourfold 2fs imperative summons שׁ֤וּבִי שׁ֨וּבִי֙ הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית שׁ֥וּבִי שׁ֖וּבִי (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier; imperative-token sweep, skeleton tier: 1 verse / 4 tokens, all in MT 7:1), a person-and-addressee shift of the tier-1 class (gendered verb forms argued from the pointed bytes and the WEB rendering “Return, return, Shulammite!” web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1; no morphology layer is staged). The rear seam is held on form, not voice: the seam verse closes כִּמְחֹלַ֖ת הַֽמַּחֲנָֽיִם (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) and the next verse opens the suffixed-body-part wasf מַה יָּפ֧וּ פְעָמַ֛יִךְ בַּנְּעָלִ֖ים בַּת נָדִ֑יב (oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, byte tier), while the 2fs address itself runs across the join from וְנֶחֱזֶה בָּ֑ךְ (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) into פְעָמַ֛יִךְ (oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, byte tier), exactly as the following shipped row Song.7.1-Song.7.5 argues the same seam from its side, so the two rows are coherent. The nadiv catchword straddle the row discloses re-sweeps to 2 verses at skeleton tier: נָדִֽיב (oshb:Song.6.12, byte tier) and בַּת נָדִ֑יב (oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, byte tier). The epithet digit decorates the addressee's uniqueness; neither seam rests on it, so the defect is a defective digit claim not alone load-bearing: medium by the severity law, not high; not low, because the claim as written is false at its named object rather than merely undigited. No parashah seg, paseq or K/Q stands at MT 7:1 (WLC inventory; absence never counterevidence). Every written dual in the row (WEB 6:13 = MT 7:1; WEB 7:1 = MT 7:2) is arithmetically right through the crosswalk, and the row's curly WEB quotation verifies verbatim at web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1. (3) Repair proposal validated as adversarially as the row: the auditor's field repair carries only digits re-derived above (exact byte token 1 verse / 1 token; prefix-tolerant skeleton 1 verse / 2 tokens, the second being the bet-prefixed form) and changes no span, so it is ENDORSED AS A PROPOSAL for owner triage, with the offset-zone dual qualifier retained on every ref it touches. Count-object item: span_change false, span_ruling n/a; both sides of the row's seams were nonetheless weighed from bytes to fix load-bearing status.

CONFIRM at medium (E-05 false exclusivity claim at the count object named, not load-bearing). Re-derived both ways from the staged bytes. (1) The row writes that the wall-noun pair חוֹמָ֣ה (oshb:Song.8.9, byte tier) / חוֹמָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) is the lexeme's only two sites in the book. Re-swept with the object named: at the plene singular SPELLING the skeleton sweep returns exactly 2 verses / 2 tokens (MT 8:9, MT 8:10), so the digit is right for that spelling; but the same lexeme's plural stands at oshb:Song.5.7 as שֹׁמְרֵ֖י הַחֹמֽוֹת (byte tier; WEB “The keepers of the walls” web:Song.5.7, so both witnesses read walls), written defective without the vav: the defective-plural skeleton returns 1 verse (MT 5:7), the plene-plural spelling with vav returns 0 verses, the construct spelling returns 0 verses, and the broad two-consonant substring sweep (7 verses) adds only unrelated lexemes (חִמַּ֣דְתִּי, מִלְחָמָ֑ה, חָמַ֣ק, מַחֲּמַדִּ֑ים, כַּֽחַמָּ֔ה, חַמּוּקֵ֣י; oshb:Song.2.3, 3.8, 5.6, 5.16, 6.10 and oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1). The wall LEXEME therefore has exactly 3 verse sites (MT 5:7, 8:9, 8:10) and the exclusivity claim is false at the object the row names: the book's own defective/plene hazard class realised, as the finding says. The pair's tier labels are right as shipped: the two tokens are byte-distinct, equal once cantillation is stripped (accent_stripped tier), skeleton-equal. (2) Not load-bearing, established from both sides of the row's back seam. The closing verse ends in the 1cp voice, נָצ֥וּר עָלֶ֖יהָ ל֥וּחַ אָֽרֶז (oshb:Song.8.9, byte tier; נִבְנֶ֥ה and נָצ֥וּר both 1cp, argued from the pointed bytes and the WEB rendering “we will build” web:Song.8.9; no morphology layer is staged), and the next verse opens on the 1cs pronoun אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier), the in-verse person change the row itself names as the seam's warrant, coherent with the following shipped row Song.8.10-Song.8.10, which argues the same seam from its own side. The byte-true straddle is disclosed, not suppressed: אִם חוֹמָ֣ה הִ֔יא (oshb:Song.8.9, byte tier) answered by אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier), and וְשָׁדַ֖יִם אֵ֣ין לָ֑הּ (oshb:Song.8.8, byte tier) answered by וְשָׁדַ֖י כַּמִּגְדָּל֑וֹת (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier). The front seam also stands from both sides: MT 8:7 closes on the impersonal gnomic בּ֖וֹז יָב֥וּזוּ לֽוֹ (oshb:Song.8.7, byte tier) under the WLC setumah at MT 8:7 (single-witness, tier-3, corroboration only), and אָח֥וֹת לָ֨נוּ֙ קְטַנָּ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.8, byte tier) opens the 1cp speaker group. The false digit decorates the straddle's rarity; a third lexeme site in the watchmen scene at MT 5:7 neither weakens the answering pair at 8:9|8:10 nor touches either seam, so the defect is a false exclusivity claim not alone load-bearing: medium by the severity law, not high; not low, because the claim is false at its named object, not merely undigited. No K/Q, paseq or parashah seg stands at MT 8:9 (WLC inventory; absence never counterevidence); the petuchah at MT 8:10, the book's only PE, belongs to the next row's close. (3) Repair proposal validated as adversarially as the row: the auditor's field repair re-cuts the object to the plene singular spelling, carries 2 verses (MT 8:9, MT 8:10) spelling-scoped, discloses הַחֹמֽוֹת (oshb:Song.5.7, byte tier) as the third lexeme site, keeps the byte / accent_stripped labels and changes no span; every digit in it re-derives above, so it is ENDORSED AS A PROPOSAL for owner triage. Count-object item: span_change false, span_ruling n/a; both sides of the row's seams were nonetheless weighed from bytes to fix load-bearing status.
